clue.text: Bribe in rather poor taste

parts.note: food in poor taste is bland, lacking flavour
the suffix -ish means rather or somewhat, as in reddish

explanation.surface: Someone offers a bribe that is a little tasteless.
explanation.definitionFit: To blandish is to coax with flattery, a soft kind of bribery to win someone over.

clue.text: Sailed away from port?

definitions.meaning: a ship that sailed away has departed or gone
port is the nautical term for the ...-hand side of a vessel

explanation.definitionFit: Departed is a past form of leave, and port is the sailor's word for the left side.

clue.text: If overturned when firm flop

indicators.note: turned upside down in a down clue, so the two letters of the word If are read the other way

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A business that collapses when one condition goes wrong is a disaster.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiasco is a humiliating failure, a complete flop.

clue.text: Writer takes wild hour with tea break

indicators.note: wild suggests letters running out of control into a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written
a tea break is a pause for a cup of tea, so it yields the drink's name

explanation.surface: An author lets an hour go by during a tea break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' signals the shuffle; 'takes' and 'with' just join. Henry David Thoreau was the American author of Walden.
explanation.definitionFit: Thoreau was an American essayist and author, best known for Walden, so he is a writer.

clue.text: In continual pain, always about the church

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for always goes round the church

parts.note: ay (also aye) is an old word for always or ever
CH is the standard abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: Someone in constant pain is forever going round the church.
explanation.definitionFit: Achy describes a body full of dull, persistent aches, so suffering continual pain.

clue.text: Transfat is unlikely to get you moving rapidly

definitions.note: a verb phrase standing for things that do this, the noun answer

indicators.note: unlikely suggests an improbable arrangement, so these letters are recast

explanation.surface: Eating trans fats will not make you any quicker on your feet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link. The definition describes what the answer does rather than naming it, a loose Gordius touch.
explanation.definitionFit: Express rail services carry passengers at high speed, so they get you moving rapidly.

clue.text: Forms of silica used by a computer expert

parts.note: Bill Gates, co-founder of Microsoft, is the best-known computer expert

explanation.surface: Silicon materials are put to work by a tech tycoon.
explanation.definitionFit: Agate is a banded variety of chalcedony, which is a form of silica; the plural matches.

clue.text: King of the elves makes nearly everyone get wealthy

indicators.note: nearly says the word for everyone stops one letter short

parts.note: all means everyone
to get, as in get rich, is to become or be
rich means wealthy

explanation.surface: A fairy monarch makes almost all his subjects prosperous.
explanation.definitionFit: In Germanic legend and Wagner's Ring, Alberich is the ruler of the elves or dwarves who forges the ring.

clue.text: Ringing tone of former primate

parts.note: Cosmo Lang was Archbishop of Canterbury, Primate of All England, 1928 to 1942; his initial gives the first letter
the surname of that archbishop, Cosmo Lang

explanation.surface: A bell's peal comes from an extinct ape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Primate' suggests an ape, but here it is the senior archbishop of the Church of England, initial plus surname.
explanation.definitionFit: A clang is a loud metallic ringing sound, like a struck bell.

clue.text: One in poor health, not strong

indicators.note: not says the letter for strong is taken away from the word before it

parts.note: unfit means in poor physical condition
F is forte, the musical direction meaning loud or strong

explanation.surface: Someone sick is unlikely to be robust.
explanation.walkthrough: F for forte is a musical abbreviation; 'strong' stands for it here.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit is a single thing, the number one in counting.

clue.text: Condition of Vatican City after reports of scandals?

definitions.text: Condition of Vatican City after reports of scandals?

parts.words: Condition of Vatican City after reports of scandals?
parts.note: the Vatican is a sovereign country, and after scandal it would be apologetic and in a poor way

explanation.surface: The Holy See is in a bad way after abuse reports.
explanation.definitionFit: A wretched condition is a common idiom for bad shape, and the Vatican is literally a contrite nation.

clue.text: Irishman said to have trouble in opera

indicators.note: said signals a word spoken rather than spelt, so only its pronunciation counts

parts.note: Mick is a stock name for an Irishman
ado means fuss or trouble

explanation.surface: An Irish fellow reportedly has difficulty at the opera.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mikado is the comic opera by Gilbert and Sullivan, set in a fanciful Japan.

clue.text: Strike of 1707?

definitions.meaning: a strike is an action taken by a trade union
in 1707 the legislation joining England and Scotland was passed

explanation.walkthrough: The 1707 statute united the Parliaments of England and Scotland into Great Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A strike is a deed of a trade union, and the 1707 statute bears this exact name.

clue.text: Printed sign of hazard with broken seat

indicators.note: a broken seat is in pieces, so its letters are reassembled

parts.note: taken as written
a hazard is a risk

explanation.surface: A printed notice warns of the danger of a broken chair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' rearranges the letters of 'seat' into ASTE; 'with' is a link, and the hazard follows in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The star-shaped typographical mark is a symbol used in printing to flag a note.

clue.text: Refrain from raising weapon

indicators.note: raising in a down clue lifts the word upward, reading the letters bottom to top

parts.note: gat is slang for a gun

explanation.surface: Avoid picking up a gun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refrain' looks like a verb, but it is the noun: a chorus. 'from' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A tag is a repeated line or chorus, the refrain of a song or speech.

clue.text: They use preparation to induce sleep

indicators.note: a preparation is something made up, so these letters are worked into a new form

explanation.surface: People take a potion to help them nod off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'They use' are seven letters to rearrange; 'to induce' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Shut-eye is informal for sleep, the time with eyes closed.

clue.text: Solver said to be classy

indicators.note: said signals that the letter is heard rather than read

parts.note: U means upper-class, from the old U and non-U distinction in British speech

explanation.surface: A puzzler is told they are posh.
explanation.walkthrough: Crosswords address the solver as 'you'. U for upper class is a British usage from 1950s talk of U and non-U manners.
explanation.definitionFit: The setter speaks to the person doing the puzzle as you, so the reader is the solver.

clue.text: A vice reportedly of Hebrew king

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard, so the phrase is spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: a vice is a gripping tool, a gripper

explanation.surface: A moral failing is said to belong to an ancient Jewish ruler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vice' suggests sin; here it is the workshop clamp. 'of' is a link. Herod Agrippa ruled Judaea.
explanation.definitionFit: Herod Agrippa I and II were kings of Judaea in Roman times.

clue.text: Leave out having a feast …

definitions.meaning: to leave out is to omit or skip over
the Jewish spring festival commemorating the Exodus

explanation.walkthrough: 'having' just joins the two senses; the dots lead to the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass over is to omit, and the Jewish festival of the Exodus has the same name.

clue.text: … and go on with what's Lent

definitions.meaning: to go on is to move forward or progress
money that is lent is a loan paid in anticipation

explanation.walkthrough: The capital on 'Lent' suggests the Christian season after a feast, but it is simply money loaned.
explanation.definitionFit: An advance is both progress forward and money paid ahead, a loan.

clue.text: Defeat scam when discovered

parts.note: a con is a swindle or scam
found means discovered

explanation.surface: A swindle is foiled once it comes to light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To confound is to thwart or defeat, as in confounding enemies.

clue.text: Oral sense of smells

definitions.meaning: said out loud, the word sense sounds like scents, which are pleasant smells
smells are aromas perceived by the nose

explanation.walkthrough: 'Oral' wants to be about the mouth; it means spoken, so 'sense' is heard as 'scents'. 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Odours are smells or scents, the things the nose detects.

clue.text: Get a thing about bosses

indicators.note: about can mean around or in a jumble, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone becomes preoccupied with their managers.
explanation.walkthrough: Gordius uses the verb intransitively: to obsess is to get a thing, a fixation.
explanation.definitionFit: To be fixated is to have a thing for something, an informal idiom.

clue.text: Group of islands off, mainly, New York perhaps …

indicators.note: off means out of order or awry, so the letters are rearranged
mainly means most of the city's name, one letter dropped

parts.note: the American city, spelt out in full

explanation.surface: A cluster of islands lies off the coast of New York.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mainly' drops W, leaving NEYORK, which 'off' rearranges. 'perhaps' and the dots lead into the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Orkney is an archipelago off the north coast of Scotland.

clue.text: Accompaniment 6 need to minimise half of 14

definitions.meaning: music that goes with a film
fast trains need a safe, solid railway to reduce risk, the second half of asterisk

explanation.walkthrough: 6 is FAST TRAINS and half of 14 (ASTERISK) is RISK.
explanation.definitionFit: A film's music runs alongside it as accompaniment, and a secure railway line is a sound track.

clue.text: … put up across East River

indicators.note: across means spread over, so the reversed word sits around the compass point
up in a down clue says the word is read from the bottom up

parts.note: set means put or placed
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: Someone sets up camp across the East River.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns SET into TES, which goes round E.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tees is a river in north-east England flowing into the North Sea.

clue.text: Article contains no lack of identification

definitions.note: a noun phrase standing for the short form of anonymous

indicators.note: contains means the first word holds the second inside it

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: This item has no named author.
explanation.definitionFit: Anon, short for anonymous, marks a work whose author is unknown or unidentified.

clue.text: Zealous saint beheaded

indicators.note: beheaded means the first letter is cut off

parts.note: St David is the patron saint of Wales

explanation.surface: A fervent martyr loses his head.
explanation.definitionFit: Avid means keen or eager, a close synonym of zealous.

clue.text: Blood factor — one noted for considerable flow

definitions.note: a phrase describing one notable river

parts.note: Rh is the rhesus factor in blood groups

explanation.surface: A blood type is known for heavy bleeding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blood' and 'flow' suggest a haemorrhage; the flow is a French river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rhone is a major European river, famous for a large volume of water.

clue.text: Parson detailed to hack Bentley's jingle

indicators.note: detailed means with its tail removed, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a parson is a cleric
to hew is to hack or chop

explanation.surface: A clergyman is assigned to cut up a car maker's advertising tune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bentley' suggests the car; it is Edmund Clerihew Bentley, inventor of the four-line comic biographical verse. 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The comic four-line verse form is named after its inventor E. C. Bentley's middle name.
